title: SkipFlow: Improving the Precision of Points-to Analysis using Primitive Values and Predicate Edges
problem: Traditional points-to analysis (Andersen/Steensgaard) loses precision by ignoring branching structure and primitive value flows, leading to unnecessary imprecision when constants flow across method boundaries.
motivation: Precise points-to analysis is crucial for closed-world binary generation (e.g., GraalVM Native Image); precision losses directly increase binary size and harm optimization.
method: SkipFlow interprocedurally tracks both primitives and objects, capturing branching structure via predicate edges without full flow-sensitivity. Two-stage approach: context-insensitive parsing, then context-sensitive refinement during inlining using call graph information.
key_novelty: Predicate edges to explicitly capture control-flow information in points-to analysis, combined with primitive value tracking for improved precision without flow-sensitivity overhead.
contributions: Lightweight points-to analysis tracking both primitives and objects
Predicate edges to capture branching structure
9% average reduction in reachable methods for microservices without significant analysis time increase
limitations: Applied only to closed-world Java scenarios; effectiveness on other languages/settings not discussed.
primary_theme: precision-improved points-to analysis for native image generation
